text:
Predicates:
Cost(x, y) ::: x costs y dollars.
Cheaper(x, y) ::: x is cheaper than y.
Provide(x, y) ::: x provides financial aid to y.
Applicant(x) ::: x is a GRE applicant.
Prove(x, y) ::: x proves y.
EconomicHardship(x) ::: x has economic hardship.
SingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
FewResources(x) ::: x has few resources available to them.
Apply(x, y) ::: x is applying to take y.
Work(x) ::: x has been out of work.

Premises:
Cost(greTest, 205) ∧ Cheaper(greTest, 300) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test, which is cheaper than $300.
∀x ((Applicant(x) ∧ Prove(x, economicHardship)) → Provide(ets, x)) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those GRE applicants who prove economic hardship.
∀x ((SingleParentFamily(x) ∨ FewResources(x)) → Prove(x, economicHardship)) ::: Those living in single-parent families or having few resources available to them can prove economic hardship.
SingleParentFamily(tom) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family.
Work(tomDad) ∧ FewResources(tom) ::: Tom's dad has been out of work, and Tom has few resources available to him.
Apply(tom, greTest) ::: Tom is applying to take the GRE test.

Conclusion:
Provide(ets, tom) ::: ETS provides financial aid to Tom.
